name: Framework Initialization Seed
description: Automatic memory seeding for new projects. Load these entries into /memories/repo/ during project initialization.

entries.title: Decision Gate: Choose Your Track
entries.content:
EVERY new ticket starts with WORKFLOW_DECISION_GATE.md. Answer 3 questions:
1. Scope Check: Is this a single file/component change?
2. Complexity Check: Does this require design/research?
3. Effort Estimate: Will this take < 30 minutes?

Answer pattern determines Track:
- All YES → Track A (Lean): 30 min overhead, quick decision→code→test→done
- Any NO → Track B (Full): 1 hour overhead, decision→requirements→design→plan→code→test→review→done

This is non-negotiable. No ticket work without decision gate. See project-management/WORKFLOW_DECISION_GATE.md

entries.title: Error Recovery Pattern: 3 Attempts, 5 Minutes Each
entries.content:
When something fails, use this pattern:

Step 1 (< 5 min): Try autonomous fixes
- Dependency issues → npm/pip/flutter install
- File not found → check path, case sensitivity
- Type errors → run build, read full error
- Auth errors → verify credentials/permissions
- Network failures → retry with backoff

Step 2 (< 5 min each, max 3 times): Adjust and retry
- Change code slightly, rebuild, test
- Check logs for more info
- Try different approach

Step 3 (No progress?): STOP and escalate
- You've hit the circuit breaker
- Document what you tried and why it failed
- Ask for human help (see EMERGENCIES.md)

NEVER retry the same command 10 times hoping for different results. That's a circuit breaker trigger.

entries.title: Circuit Breaker: When to Stop and Escalate
entries.content:
Circuit breaker triggers (escalate immediately when ANY of these occur):

1. **Repetition Without Progress**: Attempted 3 times, no measurable progress toward goal
2. **Error Pattern Repeats**: Same root cause, same error message appearing again
3. **Retry Loop**: Retrying the same command repeatedly expecting different results
4. **Cascading failures**: Fixed one thing, broke three others

Escalation format:
- Issue: [One sentence]
- What happened: [Error + stack trace]
- What I tried: [3 numbered attempts with results]
- Why escalating: [Which trigger was hit]
- Hypothesis: [What I think the real problem is]
- Recommended next steps: [What could work, even if you can't do it]

See .agent/rules/WORKFLOW.md and .agent/rules/EMERGENCIES.md

entries.title: Memory Checkpoint: Step 3 of Every Workflow
entries.content:
After completing significant work, ALWAYS ask:
"What would help the next agent do similar work faster?"

If answer is valuable, save it to /memories/repo/:
- Pattern discovered? → Save as repo memory
- Gotcha/trap found? → Save as repo memory  
- Validation method that works? → Save as repo memory
- Code style for this stack? → Save as repo memory

Format:
- Title: Specific and searchable
- Content: 3-5 sentences, actionable not theoretical
- Tags: 3-4 keywords for discovery
- Example: "Flutter TextField validation pattern" not "how to validate in Flutter"

Memory creates institutional knowledge. Each entry saves future agents 15-30 minutes.
See .agent/rules/WORKFLOW.md Step 3 and /memories/repo/ examples.

entries.title: Track A vs Track B: Quick Reference
entries.content:
TRACK A (Lean) - For simple, bounded work:
- Decision → Code → Test → Done
- 30 minutes overhead total
- Use when: single file change, no design needed, < 30 min effort
- Examples: bug fix, UI tweak, small feature

TRACK B (Full) - For complex, architectural work:
- Decision → Req → Design → Plan → Code → Test → Review → Done
- 1 hour overhead total
- Use when: new feature, design needed, > 30 min effort, multiple files
- Examples: new epic, refactor, integration

Determine track using WORKFLOW_DECISION_GATE.md (3 questions).
Don't skip phases in Track B; phases exist for a reason.
Don't over-engineer Track A work with unnecessary documentation.

Each track has appropriate ceremonies matched to work complexity.

entries.title: Bob Orchestration Commands: Quick Start
entries.content:
Bob is your command orchestrator. Key commands:

`orchestrate --single`
- Executes ONE action from the prioritized backlog
- Use when: following manual workflow, testing specific action
- Returns: action result or escalation point

`orchestrate --auto`
- Executes actions until a decision point or error is hit
- Use when: running an automated ticket phase
- Returns: when human input needed

`orchestrate --max-steps N`
- Executes up to N actions before stopping
- Use when: limiting scope of auto execution
- Safety mechanism for large changes

`orchestrate --no-prompt`
- Skips confirmation prompts, executes autonomously
- Use when: in CI/CD or batch operations
- Requires explicit approval first

Full command docs: engine/src/orchestration/types.ts
Command mapping: engine/src/shared/command_mapping.ts
See BOB_README.md for architecture details.

entries.title: Common Mistakes (Avoid These)
entries.content:
🚫 Framework Anti-Patterns:

1. **Skip Decision Gate**: Thinking you can save time. You can't. It clears confusion immediately.
2. **Mix Tracks**: Using Full workflow for Track A work (over-engineering) or Track A for Track B work (under-delivering).
3. **Ignore Circuit Breaker**: Retrying same command 10+ times. That's a loop - escalate instead.
4. **Over-Automate**: Trying to automate something that needs human judgment (architecture decisions, design choices).
5. **Forget Memory Checkpoint**: Completing work without asking "what did I learn?" Lost knowledge for next agent.
6. **Assume Parallel Execution**: Tasks aren't parallelized by default. Rare case where independent tasks happen simultaneously - document when doing it.
7. **Skip Testing**: Thinking code works so tests aren't needed. Tests are how you verify decision quality.

See .agent/rules/WORKFLOW.md Anti-patterns section for detailed explanations.

entries.title: Core Rules Architecture: 5 Essential Files
entries.content:
The framework has 5 core rule files (no more 19 with duplication):

1. **.agent/rules/CORE_PRINCIPLES.md** (Universal)
   - 8 principles: Simplicity, Self-Describing, Immutability, Composition, Testability, Errors as Data, Explicit, Separation of Concerns
   - Read once, applies to all code

2. **.agent/rules/CODE_QUALITY.md** (All code)
   - Testing requirements (TDD, 5-key-questions)
   - Code style guides (JS/TS/Python/Flutter/Dart)
   - Code review standards
   - When to escalate

3. **.agent/rules/WORKFLOW.md** (Execution)
   - Step 1: Decision Gate
   - Step 2: Error Recovery & Circuit Breaker
   - Step 3: Update Memory
   - Key Rules and Anti-patterns

4. **.agent/rules/EMERGENCIES.md** (When stuck)
   - Escalation protocol (3 steps)
   - Emergency scenarios with handling
   - Post-escalation review
   - FAQ

5. **project-management/WORKFLOW_DECISION_GATE.md** (First thing)
   - 3-question decision matrix
   - Determines Track A vs Track B
   - Mandatory before any ticket work

Stack-specific rules available: javascript.md, python.md, flutter.md, react.md, fastapi.md
See .agent/rules/CONSOLIDATION_GUIDE.md for why 19 files → 5 files consolidation happened.

entries.title: Project Initialization Checklist
entries.content:
When starting a new project, verify these are in place:

☑ WORKFLOW_DECISION_GATE.md (in project-management/)
  → Required before ANY ticket work

☑ 5 Core Rules (in .agent/rules/)
  → CORE_PRINCIPLES.md, CODE_QUALITY.md, WORKFLOW.md, EMERGENCIES.md
  → Plus CONSOLIDATION_GUIDE.md for context

☑ Repository Memory (in /memories/repo/)
  → Should have framework-decision-gate
  → Should have framework-error-recovery
  → Should have framework-circuit-breaker
  → Should have framework-memory-checkpoint
  → Should have framework-two-tracks
  → Should have framework-bob-commands
  → Should have framework-common-mistakes
  → Should have framework-rules-overview
  → (This is the memory-seed.json file)

☑ Tech Stack Verified
  → ci/ci_config.sh has correct tech stack
  → Primary testing framework installed (jest, pytest, flutter_test, etc)
  → No placeholder values in build configs

Optional but recommended:
  → BOB_README.md for orchestration docs
  → Stack-specific rules (.agent/rules/javascript.md, etc)
  → CLAUDE.md for agent interaction guidelines

All core files are in the framework root. Copy/reference them in new projects.

entries.title: Slash-command Mapping for /bob
entries.content:
In this framework `/bob` is shorthand for executing the Bob engine. The memory seeding ensures new agents know how to translate it:

- `/bob` → run `cd engine; npm run start -- bob` via run_in_terminal.
- `/bob-status` → run `cd engine; npm run start -- bob-status`.

Do NOT assume typing `/bob` executes the command automatically; an agent must explicitly call the terminal tool. The same pattern applies for any future slash-commands mapped to terminal actions.
